chosen.premise: Earthquakes send Golem rolling downhill, so people carve mountain grooves to redirect its course.
chosen.hook: People built mountain grooves to stop Golem traffic.
chosen.visualIdea: An earthquake starts the roll, then carved grooves assemble into a giant mountain guideway.
chosen.note: The most distinctive premise: Golem migration is such a recurring hazard that people carve mountain guideways to redirect it. The environmental scale and practical human response create a complete visual story.

candidates.premise: Once a year, Golem sheds its rocky shell, which crumbles into enriched soil that farmers collect.
candidates.hook: Golem’s discarded skin becomes farm fertilizer.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Golem shedding a shell, then the shell crumbling into soil spread across crop fields.
candidates.note: Highly Golem-specific and strongly supported. The farming payoff is unusual and easy to visualize, though the core molting fact may be familiar to dedicated fans.

candidates.premise: Golem can survive dynamite blasts without a scratch, yet rain and humidity bother it.
candidates.hook: Dynamite cannot hurt Golem—but rain can.
candidates.visualIdea: Split-screen: dynamite detonates harmlessly against Golem, then rain makes it recoil.
candidates.note: Excellent contradiction, directly supported by Pokédex entries, though the rain-versus-dynamite framing is more of a comparison than a uniquely complex Golem behavior.

candidates.premise: Golem detonates its own body to launch itself up steep mountain paths and between peaks.
candidates.hook: Golem reaches the next mountain by exploding itself.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate Golem crouching, detonating, and blasting upward along a steep mountain path.
candidates.note: A strong, cinematic mechanic backed by multiple entries, but self-detonating Pokémon are not entirely unique and the premise lacks a sharper contradiction or consequence.

candidates.premise: Young Golem shed their shells yearly, but ancient Golem stop shedding and grow moss-green shells.
candidates.hook: A mossy Golem may be one that stopped aging normally.
candidates.visualIdea: Cycle through yearly shell shedding, then reveal an old Golem whose shell is covered in green moss.
candidates.note: The moss-covered shell is a memorable reveal, but 'stopped aging normally' is an unsupported interpretation. The evidence only says old Golem stop shedding and develop mossy shells.

candidates.premise: Graveler reaches level 25, but becoming Golem requires a trade instead of another level.
candidates.hook: Golem’s evolution asks for a friend, not more experience.
candidates.visualIdea: A Graveler hits level 25, stops evolving, then transforms only after a trade animation.
candidates.note: Clear and accurate, but trade evolution is a familiar Pokémon mechanic and not especially surprising for experienced fans. The friend framing is editorial rather than stated by the research.
